subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Two-Stroke Engine
description: Learn The Two-Stroke Engine in one minute.

hook.text: Most engines fire every two rotations—a two-stroke fires on every single one.

buildup.text: Double the power strokes for the same speed gives two-strokes incredible power density.

discovery.text: They merge intake and exhaust into the power and compression strokes, eliminating two steps.

twist.text: Two-strokes burn oil mixed with fuel and waste unburned gas, making them dirty and inefficient.

climax.text: They dominate chainsaws and motorcycles but were banned from most cars due to pollution.

punchline.text: An engine that fires twice as often pollutes twice as much.

quiz.question: How often does a two-stroke engine fire compared to a four-stroke?

details.summary: Two-stroke engines complete a power cycle in just two piston movements instead of four, producing power every revolution for a simpler, lighter, and higher power-to-weight design that sacrifices fuel efficiency and emissions.
details.whyItMatters: Two-stroke engines are pivotal in applications where weight and simplicity matter more than efficiency, from chainsaws to motorcycles. Their high emissions have driven them out of most automotive applications.
takeaways: Power is produced every crankshaft revolution instead of every other one
They have no valves, using ports in the cylinder wall instead
Higher emissions and fuel waste led to their decline in vehicles

faq.question: Why are two-stroke engines less fuel efficient?
faq.answer: During the scavenging phase, fresh fuel-air mixture helps push exhaust out of the cylinder. Some unburned fuel escapes with the exhaust, wasting fuel and producing hydrocarbon emissions that four-strokes avoid.

faq.question: Are any companies developing clean two-stroke engines?
faq.answer: Yes. Companies are experimenting with opposed-piston two-stroke designs using direct injection and advanced scavenging. These engines could theoretically combine two-stroke power density with four-stroke-level emissions.
